doc.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Playing with Specks Red's Black band in Moline
summary: Asked whether playing with a Black band was a problem, he says no, and recalls Jo Jones hearing him later while he was with Goodman.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: When you say Specks Red, Specks Red’s band, was it a black band? white band? mixed band?
Black band. There was no trouble with you playing with the black band?

No. In fact, [Harry] Sweets [Edison] used to call me Dusty Foot. He said, “You’re not Italian. You’re a Dusty Foot.” [? ?] “You’re Arapahoe.” Okay. Jo was a real character, but I learned an awful lot from him.
How old were you when you met him?

I was about – I was in Benny Goodman’s band. I went to catch Basie’s band. He was with Basie’s band. He heard me play. He said, “You and I are going to be playing lots of stuff together in the near future.” Sure enough, it happened that way.
